newsitem.title: USA: Viacom, Seagram in settlement talk.
newsitem.headline: Viacom, Seagram in settlement talk.

text.p: The trial of the dispute between Seagram Co Limited and Viacom Inc over a joint cable venture, USA Networks, will be suspended for two days while the parties are in settlement talks, a source close to the case told Reuters.
According to the source, "There will be a hiatus to permit the parties to discuss resolution. There has been some progress on that."

In the trial which began Tuesday in the Delaware Chancery Court Seagram unit MCA Inc has asked that Viacom be required to sell off cable operations that compete with the joint venture or sell its half of the partnership to MCA.

Viacom unit, Paramount Communications Inc, has alleged there is no breach of the partnership, that the partnership is working well and that MCA is trying to get control of USA Network "at an unfairly low price", according to court documents.
After the testimony of an MCA attorney Jeffrey Nagin is completed today the trial before Vice Chancellor Myron Steele will be adjourned and will resume Thursday.
If a settlement is reached by Thursday the trial will end.
During the trial MCA witnesses have recounted the drafting of the original joint venture agreement in 1981 among MCA, Paramount and Time Inc. In 1987, Time sold its share to the remaining partners.
If the trial does continue potential witnesses include Seagram chief executive Edgar Bronfman and Viacom chairman Sumner Redstone.
